text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange rose 0.13 percent on Tuesday boosted by some of the largest capitalisation companies, including Wafabank, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 437.25 points compared with 436.70 points on Monday.
"After a slight stagnation on Monday, the market has purusued its higher trend due to blue chip active trading," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
One of the market's liquid stocks, Wafabank rose four dirhams to close at 540 dirhams.
Insistant rumours on the stock exchange predict that the bank would increase its capital as it planned to expand its branches throughout the country, the analyst said.
Fertiliser firm Fertima, recently privatised closed at 205 dirhams, up two dirhams over Monday's session, a stockbroker at Upline Securities said.
The firm's identification code FERT.CS is not available yet on Reuters screens.
Societe Cherifienne des Petroles, which is expected to be fully privatised soon, rose 21 dirhams to close at 546 dirhams.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, was traded at 500 dirhams, the same as the previous week.
ONA's subsidiary Centrale Laitiere has increased its capital to 83.9 million dirhams ($9.7 million) from 74.6 million dirhams. The increased stake was devoted to French Groupe Danone, the group said.
ONA signed an agreement to cede 20 percent of its majority stake in Centrale Laitiere to Danone in September.
Danone holds 2.74 percent of ONA's capital under an agreement signed with the group in 1994.
Among the conglomerate's most profitable firms, Centrale Laitiere had a turnover of 2.2 billion dirhams ($255 million) in 1995.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the country's second largest private group, was unchanged at 560 dirhams.

SNI posted a consolidated net profit of 378 million dirhams ($43.7 million) in 1995. It also registered a turnover of 3.8 billion dirhams in the same period to which its agro-industry companies contributed 37 percent.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, was traded at 690 dirhams, unchanged.
Traded volume on the official market was 24.9 million dirhams, from 22.6 million on Monday, a bourse official said.
